C01.title: Udaypur: Historical Memory and the Making of a Place
C01.desc: Introduce Udaypur, its historical identity, its place in regional memory, and its references in ancient texts. Establish the town's significance and the historical questions that the book seeks to answer.

subtopics.S1: Names and identity: Udayapura / Udaypur / Udaipur, eponymous founding
subtopics.S2: Introducing the place: location, administrative setting, approach
subtopics.S3: References in ancient and medieval texts and records
subtopics.S4: Regional memory: legends, local tradition, how the town is remembered
subtopics.S5: Significance: why Udaypur matters (assessments by sources)
subtopics.S6: Historical questions: debates, uncertainties, early scholarly accounts

C02.title: The Betwa Valley: Geography, Geology and Natural Environment
C02.desc: Examine the valley's rivers, topography, seasons, geological formations, forests, flora and fauna. Explain how the natural environment shaped settlement, agriculture, access to resources, and the materials available for construction.

subtopics.S1: Rivers and hydrology: Betwa, tributaries, streamflow, water bodies
subtopics.S2: Topography and geology: plateau, Vindhyan sandstone, soils, rock formations
subtopics.S3: Climate and seasons: rainfall, temperature, monsoon, long-term change
subtopics.S5: Environment and settlement: agriculture, resources, building stone, water supply

C03.title: Before Udaypur: Prehistory, Early Vidisha and the Historical Landscape of Central India
C03.desc: Trace the region from prehistory through the early historic period, with particular attention to Vidisha and the emergence of regional political and cultural networks. Introduce the trade routes, sacred centres and changing powers that formed the wider historical setting for Udaypur.

subtopics.S1: Prehistory: stone tools, rock shelters, early settlement
subtopics.S2: Early Vidisha / Besnagar: Mauryan, Śuṅga, Heliodorus pillar, Sanchi
subtopics.S3: Dasharna / Akara and ancient regional geography
subtopics.S4: Early medieval powers before the Paramāras (Guptas, Pratihāras, Kalachuris, Chandellas)
subtopics.S5: Trade routes, sacred centres and networks of Central India

C04.title: The Paramāras and the Foundation of Udaypur: Kingship, Patronage and Urban Formation
C04.desc: Examine the political development of the region, the rise of the Paramāras, the reign and legacy of Bhoja, and Udayāditya's role in establishing and shaping Udaypur. Situate the town's foundation within the history of Paramāra kingship, religious patronage and temple building, distinguishing established evidence from later tradition.

subtopics.S1: Origins and rise of the Paramāras (Agnikula, early kings, Muñja, Sindhurāja)
subtopics.S2: Bhoja: reign, conquests, learning and legacy
subtopics.S3: After Bhoja: the crisis and Udayāditya's accession, genealogy
subtopics.S4: Udayāditya's reign, wars and the foundation of Udayapura
subtopics.S5: Patronage and temple building; urban formation of Udayapura
subtopics.S6: Later Paramāras (Lakṣmadeva, Naravarman, decline) and evidence vs tradition

C05.title: The Udayeśvara Temple: Architecture, Sculpture and Religious Iconography
C05.desc: Study the temple's architectural plan, construction, stylistic features, sculptural programme, deities and iconography. Interpret the monument within the religious and artistic traditions of its period, distinguishing architectural description from interpretations of its symbolism.

subtopics.S1: Plan, layout and construction (garbhagṛha, maṇḍapa, platform, enclosure, subsidiary shrines)
subtopics.S2: Bhūmija style and śikhara; stylistic affinities and comparisons
subtopics.S4: Sculptural programme and iconography (deities, Naṭarāja, mātṛkās, dikpālas)
subtopics.S5: Śaiva meaning and symbolism (Śaiva Siddhānta interpretation)

C06.title: Inscriptions and Intellectual Life: Epigraphy, Languages and Literary Culture
C06.desc: Examine Udaypur's inscriptions, scripts, languages and epigraphic traditions, including the distinctive forms of its inscribed lettering. Use these records to investigate political authority, religious patronage, literary culture and intellectual life, while acknowledging the limits of what the evidence can establish.

subtopics.S1: The Udaipur praśasti and royal inscriptions (content, editions, dating)
subtopics.S2: The corpus of Udaypur inscriptions across centuries (Sanskrit, Persian, Hindi; pilgrim records)
subtopics.S3: Scripts and lettering: nāgarī, serpentine/nāgabandha inscriptions, grammatical charts
subtopics.S4: Languages and literary culture: Sanskrit kāvya, Bhoja's learning, scholars
subtopics.S5: What inscriptions reveal: authority, patronage, donations — and their limits

C07.title: The Wider Built Heritage of Udaypur: Fortifications, Shrines, Mosques and Water Structures
C07.desc: Document the town's surviving structures beyond the Udayeśvara temple, including fortifications, shrines, mosques, stepwells and other elements of its built heritage. Consider their dates, functions, architectural characteristics and relationship to the town's changing historical circumstances.

subtopics.S2: Other temples and shrines (Jain, Hindu, subsidiary)
subtopics.S4: Water structures: stepwells, tanks, wells, baolis
subtopics.S5: Palaces, havelis, domestic architecture, town fabric

C08.title: Religion and the Material Life of Udaypur: Ritual, Agriculture, Trade and Craft
C08.desc: Explore Śaiva traditions, ritual practices and religious institutions alongside agriculture, wells, markets, crafts, trade and patronage. Investigate the relationship between religious life and the local economy through available historical, epigraphic, archaeological and ethnographic evidence.

subtopics.S1: Śaiva traditions and sects (Pāśupata, Śaiva Siddhānta, ascetics, maṭhas)
subtopics.S2: Ritual and worship at the temple (pūjā, festivals, priests)
subtopics.S3: Temple institutions and endowments (grants, land, temple economy)
subtopics.S5: Markets, trade, crafts and artisans (stone carving, weaving)

C09.title: Society and Cultural Life: Communities, Languages, Festivals and Oral Traditions
C09.desc: Examine community identities, spoken languages, everyday customs, festivals, folklore and oral histories. Bring historical evidence into conversation with residents' memories and contemporary practices, distinguishing documented events from traditions whose historical origins remain uncertain.

subtopics.S2: Spoken languages and dialects (Bundeli, Malvi, Urdu)
subtopics.S5: Food, music, dress and material culture

C10.title: Political Change and Economic Decline: Udaypur under Successive Regimes
C10.desc: Trace the political transitions that affected Udaypur and investigate changes in its economic and regional significance. Assess the evidence for shifts in trade, patronage, settlement and institutional life rather than attributing decline to a single conquest or political event.

subtopics.S1: End of Paramāra rule; Delhi Sultanate and Malwa Sultanate
subtopics.S4: Colonial period and the princely state; Bhilsa district
subtopics.S5: Evidence of economic change, decline and depopulation

C11.title: Udaypur in the Modern Period: Archaeology, Heritage Administration and Conservation
C11.desc: Examine archaeological investigations, heritage legislation, restoration, repairs and the development of official monument status, with particular attention to the period after Indian independence. Consider how archaeological and administrative interventions have shaped the interpretation, management and conservation of Udaypur's historic sites.

subtopics.S1: Early surveys and scholarship (Cunningham, Beglar, Kielhorn, Gwalior Archaeology Dept)
subtopics.S2: Protection and legislation (ASI, protected monument status)
subtopics.S4: Heritage listing and documentation (INTACH, state archaeology)

C12.title: Udaypur Today: A Living Community and Its Historic Environment
C12.desc: Present Udaypur as a living settlement rather than merely an archaeological site. Explore contemporary livelihoods, community relationships with historic monuments, local aspirations and the practical tensions between conservation and everyday life, drawing on Udaypur Jagta Hua Kasba and other relevant sources.

subtopics.S4: Aspirations, voices and tensions between conservation and daily life

C13.title: Afterword. Conserving Udaypur: Community, Heritage and the Future
C13.desc: Reflect on the future of Udaypur and the possibilities for combining heritage conservation with local well-being. Consider the roles of residents, conservation professionals, researchers, administrators and visitors, with emphasis on realistic interventions, community participation and sustainable stewardship.

subtopics.S3: Roles of institutions, professionals and researchers
subtopics.S5: Vision for the future of the town
